outcome_verbatim: "Current work status was coded as working or not working. Information about current job was obtained, including title, employer, duties, hours worked/week, and monthly earnings." Cells summed: "Of the 456 participants, 257 (56.4%) were working at both assessments, 148 (32.4%) were not working at either assessment, 21 (4.6%) were working at baseline but not follow-up, and 30 (6.6%) were not working at baseline but were employed at follow-up."
source_locator: Methods 2.3.2 Current work status, p. 473; Results 3.1 Consistency in work status, p. 474; Table 1, p. 475
derivation_justification: Results 3.1 (p. 474) partitions all 456 analysed participants into four printed, mutually exclusive and exhaustive cells: working at both assessments 257, not working at either 148, working at baseline but not at follow-up 21, not working at baseline but employed at follow-up 30. 257+148+21+30 = 456 exactly, and each cell's printed percentage reproduces on 456 (56.4, 32.4, 4.6, 6.6, summing to 100.0). Working at the 12-month follow-up is exactly the union of the two cells that are working at follow-up: 257 + 30 = 287 of 456. Table 1 (p. 475) corroborates the partition by urban/rural: not working at both 148 = 112+36, working at either 51 = 35+16, working at both 257 = 125+132, and 272+184 = 456. The 51 in Table 1's 'working at either assessment' row equals the 21+30 of the text. NO PERCENTAGE WAS BACK-CALCULATED: every input is a printed count. The abstract's 'over 60% employed at baseline and follow-up assessment' is consistent (287/456 = 62.9 per cent at follow-up; 278/456 = 61.0 per cent at baseline).
notes: ZERO SEPARABILITY: satisfied exactly. The two cells not summed (148 not working at either assessment, 21 working at baseline but not follow-up) are precisely the people NOT working at follow-up, so zero work at 12 months is fully separable from every cell containing work at 12 months. This is the opposite of the rautio2016 case in D12.3. | CHECKED_BY IS BLANK: no independent human has checked this arithmetic yet, which is Stage G's job. Recorded in unresolved_queries.md rather than filled with a placeholder. | CONSTRUCT CAVEAT, please read before pooling: the paper never states that all work counted was remunerated. Two things support paid_any. First, the analysis deliberately excluded the one participant 'working as a volunteer' and the two full-time students, so unpaid activity and education are not in the numerator. Second, monthly earnings were obtained for every worker. But the paper also says 'To calculate monthly income of participants working in family-run businesses who were not paid separate wages, total family income was divided by the number of family members working', and 97 of the 257 employed at both assessments worked for family (Table 1, p. 475), rising to 83 of 132 rural participants. Family-business work without separate wages is economically productive and income was attributed to it, but a reviewer who reads paid_any strictly as wages or salary received personally would code this unclear. Flagged in unresolved_queries.md. | DENOMINATORS: 550 entered at baseline; 459 (83.5 per cent) completed the follow-up interview; 3 of those 459 were removed from the analyses (2 full-time students, 1 volunteer), leaving 456. 137 follow-up interviews were by telephone rather than in person. | MODERATORS: mean_age 39.12 and perc_female 42.5 are on the 459 completers, NOT the 456 analysed, and the source prints only '57.5% were male', so perc_female is the complement of a printed percentage and no counts are recoverable; n_female is therefore left blank rather than reconstructed. n_employed_baseline 278 = 257+21 from the same printed partition, on the 456 denominator. perc_post_secondary is not recoverable: education appears only in Table 2 for the unemployed-at-baseline subgroup.

source_locator: Table 1, p. 4; Methods, Participants and outcome definitions, p. 3; Results, p. 3
notes: CONSTRUCT: a COMPOSITE, confirmed. 'working (full-time or part-time work) or studying' names work and education but not training, so paid_or_education, not paid_or_education_or_training and certainly not paid_any. It never enters the primary pool. The definition also carries an unusual extra condition, 'and not being on sick leave', which removes people who hold a job but are signed off from it, so the composite is narrower than work-or-study alone in one direction and broader in another. No paid-work-only count is printed anywhere in the report. | COUNTS: Table 1 prints 'Working or studying 26/53 (49.1%)'; 26/53 = 49.1 per cent, consistent. This row's arithmetic checks out even though a neighbouring row in the same table does not, see inconsistencies.md. | TIMEPOINT: 12 months from cohort entry. The study protocol 'included follow-ups after 2 and 12 months', and the outcome is measured 'at the time of the 1-year interview'. The paper's own analytical baseline is the 2-month assessment, so the interval between the paper's two assessments is 10 months, but elapsed time since first psychiatric treatment contact, which is cohort entry, is 12 months. Either reading falls in the 9 to 18 month window and 12 is the honest figure. | DENOMINATORS: n_entered is BLANK because the size of the recruited Helsinki Early Psychosis Study cohort is never printed. Baseline cognitive testing data were available for 67, and 54 had both baseline cognitive and 1-year clinical data; the 54 is therefore itself a data-availability subset of an unstated whole, which limits the SAP section 6 bounding analyses. Small sample confirmed. | MODERATORS: mean_age 26.7 (SD 5.5) and n_female 24 of 54 are on the 54-patient Table 1 sample, one more than the 53 in the outcome denominator. perc_post_secondary is not recoverable: education is reported only as mean years, 14.5 (SD 3.4). perc_employed_baseline is not reported at all. | DIAGNOSIS: schizophrenia spectrum 32 (59.3 per cent), affective psychosis 12 (22.2), other psychotic disorder 10 (18.5); all 54 are first-episode psychosis, so 100 per cent carry a qualifying diagnosis under SAP section 7.
